summary: RepoLadder turns a TypeScript or JavaScript repo into a drill-down architecture diagram. It reads the code for facts (files, imports, calls, databases), lets Claude group and name the parts, then lays out one board per group and writes a single self-contained page you can click through.

actors.name: Developer
actors.summary: Runs RepoLadder on their own repo to get a map of it.

actors.name: Claude
actors.summary: Reads the digest of facts and groups and names the parts.

actors.name: New teammate
actors.summary: Opens the published diagram to learn how the repo fits together.

narrative: A [[developer]] points the [[src-cli|command line]] at their code.
It [[src-analyze|reads the repo]] for plain facts: which files exist and what connects to what.
[[claude]] reads a short digest of those facts and names the parts, and the [[src-model|model]] checks every name against the facts.
The [[src-build|drawing step]] lays out one board per part and packs it all into a single page.
A [[reader|new teammate]] opens that page in the [[src-viewer|viewer]] and clicks down level by level.

tours.title: Reading a repo
captions: You run the RepoLadder command on a repo. Its first stage reads the code into facts: files, imports, pages, endpoints and database use.
The analysis lists and parses every file, then asks the store finder which database collections each file reads and writes.
For every collection it finds, the store finder works out the fields the code writes and queries, so a database box can list them.

tours.title: Laying out a board
captions: Once the boards are rolled up, the command lays each one out: box sizes, lanes for the parts elsewhere, and room for labels.
Layout hands every board to a pool of D2 workers, which place the boxes and route the arrows, and caches each result.

tours.title: Opening a box in the viewer
captions: The diagram page starts the viewer, which hands every click and key to navigation.
Double-clicking a box makes navigation open its board, and the board is drawn from scratch: boxes, cylinders, wires and labels.
Each arrow's path comes from the curve helpers, which round D2's routed points into smooth wires.

children.name: Command line
children.summary: The RepoLadder command: analyze a repo, print the digest Claude reads, and build the diagram page. It runs each stage in order.

children.name: Reading the repo
children.summary: Reads the source code and writes down plain facts: which files exist, what imports what, which pages and endpoints there are, and which services and databases the code uses.

children.name: Files & imports
children.summary: Lists the source files, detects packages, and parses every file with the TypeScript compiler to resolve its imports. index.ts runs the whole analysis.

children.name: Pages & endpoints
children.summary: Finds the app's pages and server endpoints (Next.js, Express-style routes, cloud functions) and matches string literals in the code to them as runtime calls.

children.name: Services & databases
children.summary: Maps SDK imports to outside services, and finds every database read and write per collection or table, with the fields used.

children.name: Building the model
children.summary: Checks Claude's grouping against the facts and rolls the file-level facts up into one board per group, with the story, tours and flows that guide a reader.

children.name: Grouping & digest
children.summary: The schemas, glob matching, the default folder grouping and its validation, the depth rules, and the digest Claude reads before it writes a grouping.

children.name: Boards & rollup
children.summary: Rolls imports, calls and database use up to the boxes on each board, and builds the file and database boards with their code snippets.

children.name: Story, tours & flows
children.summary: Validates the story board, places each guided tour step on a board, and finds the flows: chains of arrows from an entry point to a service or store.

children.name: Drawing the diagram
children.summary: Lays out every board, measures the result for defects and readability, and packs everything into one small self-contained page.

children.name: Laying out boards
children.summary: Writes each board as D2 source and lays it out on a pool of workers, with the lane of outside boxes and the special layouts for file, database and story boards.

split.name: D2 boards
split.summary: Writes a board as D2 source and compiles it on a pool of workers, cached by source.

split.name: Lane & spacing
split.summary: Puts outside boxes in a lane at the board's edge and keeps stacked databases apart.

split.name: File, store & story boards
split.summary: The layouts for boards that aren't groups: a leaf's files, a database's collections and the story board.

children.name: Other layout engines
children.summary: Alternative layout engines (ELK and a column layout) behind one interface, used to compare against D2.

children.name: Layout checks
children.summary: The layout lint (overlaps, wires through boxes, label collisions) and the digestibility budget that says when a board needs another rung.

children.name: Page & export
children.summary: Bundles the viewer, packs the page data small, writes the self-contained HTML page, and exports boards as standalone images.

children.name: Diagram viewer
children.summary: The interactive page a reader clicks through: it draws each board, opens deeper rungs, pans and zooms, and explains any box or arrow with its evidence.

children.name: Startup & page data
children.summary: Boots the page: unpacks the viewer itself and the compressed page data, starts the viewer, and holds the shared state: the current board and selection.

split.name: Boot & state
split.summary: The page's one script, the viewer's entry point, its shared state and its color tokens.

split.name: Unpacking the data
split.summary: Decodes the packed page data: basE91 text, inflate, and the wire format back into boards.

children.name: Drawing boards
children.summary: Turns a laid-out board into SVG: box shapes, arrows and their labels.

children.name: Boxes & shapes
children.summary: Draws the boxes: one silhouette per kind, database cylinders with their collections, icons, and arrow weights.

children.name: Arrows & labels
children.summary: Arrow curves, wires the layout did not route, and placing labels so they don't collide.

children.name: Moving around
children.summary: Everything about getting around the diagram: opening rungs, going back, links, panning and zooming.

children.name: Opening boards
children.summary: Shows a board and handles clicks and keys, animates the zoom between rungs, remembers history for Back, jumps across branches, and searches.

children.name: Breadcrumbs & links
children.summary: Shows where you are (breadcrumbs and depth) and keeps a shareable link to the current board and selection.

children.name: Pan, zoom & fit
children.summary: Pans and zooms the board, fits it to the screen, zooms to a selection, and clears it on an empty click.

children.name: Detail dial
children.summary: Lets the reader choose how much a board shows: a dial of stops, from fewest boxes to everything, where boards are rolled up or opened in the browser to fit a box budget and laid out on demand. Travel animates the move between boards.

children.name: Stops & the tree
children.summary: The dial's stops and the tree of fine and coarse nodes each stop shows, with the stores and the story cut.

children.name: Fitting & travel
children.summary: Rolls boards up or opens them in the browser to fit a box budget, lays them out on demand, and animates the travel between boards.

children.name: Side panel & legend
children.summary: The panel that explains a selected box or arrow with its evidence, plus the legend and its filters.

children.name: Story, tours & reading
children.summary: The guided parts: the story board with its actors, tours, and the board walkthrough that steps through flows with a pulse along each arrow.

split.name: Story board
split.summary: The board above the parts: actors, their arrows and the narrative.

split.name: Guided tours
split.summary: Plays a tour step by step across boards.

split.name: Board walkthrough
split.summary: Steps through a board's flows, or its layers, with a pulse along each arrow.

children.name: Developer tools
children.summary: Tools for working on RepoLadder itself: the bundle build, the diagram gallery and screenshots, and the usage-ping server.

children.name: Build, gallery & shots
children.summary: Builds the plugin bundle, builds the gallery of real repos, takes screenshots of every board, and runs the layout lint.

children.name: Usage ping server
children.summary: The small Cloudflare Worker behind the opt-in usage ping: it counts runs and stores nothing about the repo.
